faq: Which tools can you send data to?
Google Sheets, Excel online, Airtable, Notion databases, common SQL databases and many CRMs. If your tool has a connection we can use, we will confirm it before you order.
Will it overwrite my existing data?
Not unless you want it to. We agree whether new data is added, merged or updated, and we test on a copy first so your live sheet is never the experiment.
Can the same result go to two places?
Yes. The Standard package covers two destinations and Premium four, for example a sheet for the team and a database for reporting.
What if a value does not fit a column?
It is saved to an errors tab with the reason, so nothing is lost and a person can correct it. The rest of the batch continues normally.

desc:
Send results to sheets, databases and tools so processed data lands where your team already works. Ecom Swift LLC maps each result to the right columns in Google Sheets, Excel, Airtable, a SQL database or your CRM, and keeps new rows arriving by themselves.

## What does it mean to send results to a sheet, database or tool?

It means delivering processed data to its final home in a form people can use. After a document is read or a record is checked, the result is written to a destination: a new row in a spreadsheet, an updated record in a CRM or a line in a database table. Each value goes into a named column with a defined format.

This is the delivery step. Without it, even perfect results sit in a file that someone must open, copy from and paste elsewhere.

## Why results trapped in files go unused

A common pattern is that processing works, then the output is a CSV in a folder. Somebody has to download it, open it, adjust the columns and paste rows into the real sheet. That person forgets one week, and the sheet is a week behind. Or they paste over existing rows and lose notes a colleague added.

Mismatched formats are another trap. A date arrives as text, a price as a string with a currency symbol, a postal code loses its leading zero. Totals fail, filters miss rows and reports show errors that have nothing to do with the business.

## How good delivery supports daily decisions

When results arrive on their own, in the right place and format, the sheet becomes something people trust. Team members open it knowing it reflects the latest data, so decisions are made from one shared source rather than several versions. Update rules keep existing rows current instead of creating repeats, and summary tabs give totals without extra work.

Time saved comes from removing copying, reformatting and reconciling. The size of that saving depends on how often data arrives and how many places it must reach. Sending the same result to two destinations, such as a sheet and a CRM, also removes the double entry that creates mismatches.

## What a good output set-up includes

- A written field map showing each source value and its destination column.
- Correct data types: real dates, numbers and text, not everything as text.
- New rows added in the right place, at the right moment.
- Update rules that change an existing row when the same item appears again.
- Optional duplicate protection based on a key such as an order or invoice number.
- A separate tab or table for rows that failed, with the reason.
- A summary tab with totals and counts for quick reading.
- Colour rules and filters, so rows needing review stand out.
- Support for scheduled updates or instant updates, depending on need.
- Handover notes that explain the layout and who to ask when it changes.

## How we do it

We start with the destination, not the data. You show us the sheet, database or tool people actually use, and we note its columns, formats and any rules. Then we compare it with the incoming data and decide how each value maps across.

We build the delivery step, then test with real results, checking that dates, numbers and text are formatted correctly and that a second run does not duplicate rows. The Basic package sends results to one sheet with a clear column layout. Standard supports two destinations, updates to existing rows, a summary tab and an error tab. Premium covers up to four destinations including Airtable, SQL or a CRM, with choices between scheduled and instant updates, review colour rules and a field map in the handover.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which column is the unique key for each record.
- Keep a spare copy of the destination sheet before the first live run.
- Use the same column names that your team already knows.
- Let failed rows go to their own tab and review that tab.
- Tell us before you rearrange columns in a live sheet.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting formulas over columns that the flow writes to.
- Sending data to a sheet that many people edit freely without protection.
- Storing numbers and dates as plain text.
- Overwriting old rows without an update rule you understand.
- Adding extra destinations before the first one is working properly.

## Who this service is for

It suits an operations lead who wants extracted orders to appear in a team sheet automatically. It suits a small business that keeps customers in a CRM and needs processed forms added there. It also suits an analyst who needs clean, regular data in a database table to feed a dashboard.

## What we need from you

Send a link or copy of each destination, a sample of the data that will be sent and a note on who uses it. Tell us which columns must never be changed. We never need your passwords. Access is given by inviting us as an editor, collaborator or developer user on the specific sheet, base or tool, and you can remove it whenever the work is complete.
